decisions.reason: The vertigo combination tablet sits close to the firm's core prescription portfolio, launched only in 2024, and has its own product page, so withdrawal within a year is unlikely.

The generic antidepressant is distant from the core offer and faces reimbursement-driven price pressure, but registration costs are already sunk and it was presented prominently, so the firm will likely keep it for now.
The combination antihypertensive line with several strengths fits the firm's established cardiovascular-style prescription offer and supports adherence, making it a strategic keeper.

The bone and joint supplement supports the strategy of pharmacy-exclusive self-care products and costs little to keep, though its low website visibility suggests a modest role and a somewhat higher risk of being dropped.
